bucket_reason: Low confidence at observe: the local rules are exact, but the cycle-level rules and the non-halting argument are open, so proof work waits.
question: W4-6 and its E-start twin (740 line 612) are a nested wall-bouncer with a clean 2^(j+1)-periodic hierarchy: fund a ~2 h wall-model stage, run only a bigger CTL search in the background, or park both?

options.label: Fund one ~2 h wall-model stage for both lines
options.consequence: Build an abstract simulator on K(n; a) from R1-R11/L1-L3 plus a ruled right-end routine, check it against the TM to 1e11 for both starts, then derive the cycle map and look for the carry invariant (a1 >= 1, wall spacing). Output: an exact model and a go/no-go on proof.md; no invariant guaranteed.

options.label: Bigger CTL sweep in the background only
options.consequence: No agent analysis; one ctlx process runs ~100 more parameter sets (longer NG/RWL_mod windows, under the 6 GB cap). A certificate would close both lines via solve_cert; 25 sets have already failed.

options.label: Park both now
options.consequence: No compute. Both lines go to STUCK at observe with these notes, rules and the 1e11 data; resume if a multi-level-counter method appears elsewhere.

rationale: Local rules cover all but the right-end routine; a_j is exactly 2^(j+1)-periodic, so a counter, not a cryptid.
One model serves 2 holdouts (same table, orbits equal from entry 2 on).
400 random K(n; a) with a1 >= 1 never halted in 2e7 steps: a wide safe set favours an invariant.

evidence.text: Fig 2: walls per cycle; the walls next to the buffer wiggle fastest, deep walls are frozen.
20 local rules, 6,000/6,000 random-context checks; 9.29M rule applications cover the blank run to 2e7 apart from the edge step, C-at-double-wall (now R11) and ~600 right-end steps.
a_j has period 2^(j+1) for j = 1..8 (k = 1e5..2.2e5); right-end reaches at 3520 + 8192(2^m - 1); no halt to 1e11.
